section.title: Introduction and Overview
section.p: CCres converts two RISC OS binary resource formats into a stable textual form and can reconstruct the binary files from that text. The supported binary formats are Toolbox Resource files with filetype ,fae and Wimp Template files with filetype ,fec.

The textual form is intended for editing, comparison, searching, translation, and bulk maintenance. It names object classes, field names, symbolic flags, and string contents explicitly, so changes that are awkward in binary editors can be made with ordinary text tools. The text syntax is close to C structure initialiser style, but remains line-oriented and simple enough to be generated and parsed without a full compiler front end.
This manual describes the standalone command-line program ccres, which performs the same conversions without requiring a desktop application.

subsection.title: Command-line behaviour
subsection.p: The command-line program normally takes two positional arguments: an input filename and an output filename. The input file type is detected from its contents, not from its name. Two options instead write a skeleton of the text format; they are described under Command-line usage.

definition.name: Toolbox Resource binary
definition.extra: First word is RESF and version is 101

definition-table.definition: Converted to text. The generated text begins with RESF:1.01.

definition.name: Wimp Template binary
definition.extra: Second, third, and fourth header words are zero

definition-table.definition: Converted to text. The generated text begins with Template:.

definition.name: Text file
definition.extra: First sixteen bytes contain no control characters other than LF

definition-table.definition: The first line selects the output binary format. RESF:1.01 selects Toolbox Resource output; Template: selects Wimp Template output.

subsection.p: When the input is text, only two text headers are recognised: RESF:1.01 and Template:. Although older descriptive material mentions RESF version 1.00, the current implementation accepts and writes only RESF version 1.01.

The program recognises text by scanning the first sixteen bytes for control characters. The binary resource and template probes are performed before that text test, so binary files are not mistaken for text merely because their filenames end in .txt.

Problems in a text file are reported on standard error with the line they are on, as Line n: message. An error, such as an unknown flag or value (which names the field it is in), a missing field or a missing brace, makes the program exit with a failure status, even though an output file may have been written. A warning, which begins Warning: , reports something the program has worked around, such as a buffer size increased to hold its text or a name truncated to fit its field, and does not change the exit status.

subsection.title: Overall text grammar
subsection.p: CCres text is line-oriented. During import, linefeeds are replaced internally with string terminators, so each source line is parsed independently. Object bodies are enclosed in braces and nested objects are represented by nested brace blocks.

p.extended-example:
resource-file ::= "RESF:1.01" LF { resource-object }
template-file ::= "Template:" LF { wimp-window } { template-font-data }
resource-object ::= object-name "{" LF { entry-line | nested-object } "}" LF
wimp-window ::= "wimp_window" "{" LF { entry-line | "wimp_icon" block } "}" LF
template-font-data ::= "template_font_data" "{" LF { entry-line } "}" LF
entry-line ::= entry-name ":" value LF
comment ::= "#" text-to-end-of-line

subsection.p: Object names are matched case-insensitively. Entry names should be written exactly as CCres emits them. The parser for entries is effectively case-sensitive at the first character and is designed around the canonical lower-case spellings shown in this chapter.

Within an object body, a colon introduces the value for that entry and causes the remainder of the line to be treated as data. A number sign introduces a comment and causes the remainder of the line to be ignored. Because values and comments consume the rest of the line, braces inside them do not affect object nesting.

subsection.title: Numbers, expressions, and symbolic values
subsection.p: Numeric fields accept more than plain decimal. The shared number parser understands:

definition-table.definition: Unsigned or signed decimal integer.
Hexadecimal integer.
Hexadecimal integer.
Hexadecimal integer.
Binary integer.
Explicit decimal integer.

subsection.p: Fields of type cmp, bbox, and coord are evaluated as arithmetic expressions rather than simple integers. The operators (), +, -, *, and / are supported. Division is integer division. Expression depth is deliberately small and malformed expressions are reported with a line number.

Many fields use symbolic values instead of raw numbers. Flag fields accept one or more symbolic names separated by vertical bars. Enumeration fields accept a single symbolic name. Residual flag bits that do not correspond to a known symbol are written as 0x... on export and may be read back in that form.
Component-reference fields accept either a numeric component id or the special names toolbox_NULL_COMPONENT and toolbox_WINDOW_FOCUS.

subsection.title: Strings, quoting, and size fields
subsection.p: CCres always exports strings in double quotes. Import does not require quotes, but quoted strings are the canonical form and should be preferred.

Quoted strings may have spaces after the closing quote. Unquoted strings run to the end of the line. Quotes are mainly significant for preserving trailing spaces unambiguously. Unmatched quotes are reported as an input error.
The textual format uses several kinds of string field:

definition-table.definition: Stored in the object's message string table. The associated ..._limit: field may be a number or *.
Stored in the object's ordinary string table. Associated limits behave the same way as message-table strings.
Stored inside a Template window's trailing string area and terminated with carriage return in the binary file.
Stored directly in the structure body. Template names are limited by the binary field width.

subsection.p: For Resource strings, a limit field of * means "allocate only enough space for the current string plus its terminator". If the string is empty and the limit is *, CCres may omit the stored string reference entirely.

For Template strings, the exported size is the allocated byte count in the Template string area. A limit of * means "use the current string length including its carriage-return terminator". If a supplied size is smaller than the string actually needs, CCres increases it and emits a warning rather than silently truncating the data. The warning does not make the conversion fail. There is no fixed limit on the size of an indirected buffer.

subsection.p: A Resource text file begins with RESF:1.01 followed by zero or more top-level Toolbox objects. Each object has a class-specific object name and contains a common object header followed by class-specific entries.

subsection.p: The fields of each kind of block are listed below, generated from the converter's own tables, followed by an example with every field at its zero value. Every field listed for a block must be present, even when its value is not used: a missing field is reported as Missing entry and the conversion fails. The fields of a block may be given in any order, but all of them must come before any nested blocks (such as gadgets, icons or menu entries), as the search for a field stops at the end of the first nested block. Fields that are only used in one form of a block (an icon with indirected text, for example) say so. A field which takes a string has a limit field, which gives the size of the buffer for it; * makes the buffer just large enough for the text given.

Flags are written as names separated by |, and any bits without a name are written in hexadecimal, as 0xvalue, so that they convert back unchanged. Where two names are listed for the same value, either is accepted, and the first is written.

subsection.title: Wimp Template text format
subsection.p: A Template text file begins with the literal line Template:. The normal canonical order is:

item.p: One or more top-level wimp_window blocks.
Zero or more top-level template_font_data blocks.

subsection.p: CCres counts top-level brace blocks before conversion, then performs a first pass that consumes only leading wimp_window blocks. For that reason, Template text should keep all window blocks before any template_font_data blocks and should not place other top-level object names in the file.
The fields of each kind of Template block follow, in the same form as those of the Resource blocks.

subsubsection.title: wimp_window
subsubsection.p: Each wimp_window block begins with template_name: and then carries the embedded Wimp window definition.

subsubsection.p: To show a sprite whose name differs from the text, the icon must be indirected, so that its validation string can name the sprite with the S command; a second name, after a comma, is used while the icon is selected. The text part always has its background filled, so an anti-aliased text and sprite icon should not also be filled. This table is from the RISC OS Programmer's Reference Manual (Wimp_CreateIcon). Pyromaniac's icon plotting, which follows RISC OS Classic, also centres text alone vertically whatever the V flag, while a sprite alone is placed at the bottom unless V is set.

subsection.title: Round-tripping and canonical output
subsection.p: CCres does not attempt byte-for-byte recreation of files created by other tools. It recreates equivalent Resource or Template content in its own normal serialisation.
Important consequences of that normalisation are:

item.p: Resource relocation entries are written in ascending offset order.
Superfluous fields that some GUI editors save are omitted when CCres does not use them.
Template text is truncated at the first control character terminator; stray bytes after a terminator are ignored when exporting to text.
Strings are re-emitted in quoted canonical form, and size fields may be normalised to * when they match the minimal required allocation.

subsection.p: For these reasons, binary comparison against an original editor-produced file is not a reliable validation method. The canonical validation loop is text-to-binary-to-text round-tripping and comparison of the textual forms.

section.title: Command-line usage
section.p: The standalone program is invoked as:

infile must be a Toolbox Resource binary, a Wimp Template binary, or a CCres text file beginning with RESF:1.01 or Template:. outfile receives the converted form. When the input is binary, the output is text. When the input is text, the output is either a Resource binary or a Template binary according to the first line of the file.

The program performs a single conversion in the direction implied by the input file. Binary Resource files and binary Template files are converted to text. Text files are converted back into binary using their first line as the format selector.
A skeleton of the text format, holding one of every kind of block with every field, can be written with:

--skeleton resource writes a Resource text file with one object of every class, each at its usual version; its window holds a keyboard shortcut and one gadget of every class, and its menu a text entry and a sprite entry. --skeleton template writes a Template text file with one window holding an icon for each kind of icon data, and a font entry. Every field is at its zero value, and the file converts to a binary file and back unchanged, so it is a starting point for writing a new file.

--describe writes the same text with comment lines, beginning #@, after each field. These give the field's type, its limit or size field, and the names and values of its flags or enumeration; they are ignored when the file is converted. The field reference in this manual is generated from them.
With any other arguments, the program prints a short usage summary and exits with a failure status.

subsection.title: Converting a Toolbox Resource file to text
subsection.p: This is the normal editing path for a Toolbox Resource file.

subsection.title: A minimal Resource text file
subsection.p: This example shows the required outer structure of a Resource text file.

p.extended-example:
RESF:1.01
window_object {
header_flags:
version:102
object_name:"Main"
window_flags:
help_message:""
help_limit:*
sprite_name:""
pointer_limit:0
hotspot:0,0
menu_name:""
default_focus:toolbox_NULL_COMPONENT
show_action:
hide_action:
toolbar_ibl:""
toolbar_itl:""
toolbar_ebl:""
toolbar_etl:""
window.visible:0,0,640,480
window.xscroll:0
window.yscroll:0
window.next:wimp_TOP
window.flags:wimp_WINDOW_MOVEABLE | wimp_WINDOW_NEW_FORMAT
window.title_fg:wimp_COLOUR_BLACK
window.title_bg:wimp_COLOUR_LIGHT_GREY
window.work_fg:wimp_COLOUR_BLACK
window.work_bg:wimp_COLOUR_VERY_LIGHT_GREY
window.scroll_outer:wimp_COLOUR_CREAM
window.scroll_inner:wimp_COLOUR_ORANGE
window.highlight_bg:wimp_COLOUR_LIGHT_GREY
window.extra_flags:
window.extent:0,-480,640,0
window.title_flags:wimp_ICON_TEXT | wimp_ICON_INDIRECTED
window.work_flags:
window.sprite_area:&ffffffff
window.xmin:0
window.ymin:0
window.title_text:"Main window"
window.title_text_limit:*
window.title_valid:""
}

subsection.title: A minimal Template text file
subsection.p: This example shows the required outer structure of a Template text file.

p.extended-example:
Template:
wimp_window {
template_name:"Main"
visible:0,0,640,480
xscroll:0
yscroll:0
next:wimp_TOP
window_flags:wimp_WINDOW_MOVEABLE | wimp_WINDOW_NEW_FORMAT
title_fg:wimp_COLOUR_BLACK
title_bg:wimp_COLOUR_LIGHT_GREY
work_fg:wimp_COLOUR_BLACK
work_bg:wimp_COLOUR_VERY_LIGHT_GREY
scroll_outer:wimp_COLOUR_CREAM
scroll_inner:wimp_COLOUR_ORANGE
highlight_bg:wimp_COLOUR_LIGHT_GREY
extra_flags:
extent:0,-480,640,0
title_flags:wimp_ICON_TEXT | wimp_ICON_INDIRECTED
work_flags:wimp_BUTTON_CLICK
sprite_area:&1
xmin:0
ymin:0
text.text:"Main window"
text.size:12
text.validation:""
}

revision.author: Dave Appleby
revision.title: Original CCres releases up to v1.08
revision.change: Created and maintained the original CCres implementation through version 1.08, distributed as FreeWare.

revision.author: John Tytgat / BASS
revision.title: Version 1.09 released
revision.change: Prepared the first BASS-maintained public source and binary release.
Changed the CCres licence to the GNU General Public License.

revision.author: John Tytgat / BASS
revision.title: Version 1.10 released
revision.change: Stopped Template icons without the Text and Sprite bit set from reporting a harmless unexpected flag-combination error.

revision.author: John Tytgat / BASS
revision.title: Version 1.11 released
revision.change: Added version and syntax reporting when the program is run without parameters in a TaskWindow or outside the Desktop.
Added four missing Iconbar flags.
Made uncovered flag bits report the error "Not all bits are covered".

revision.author: John Tytgat / BASS
revision.title: Version 1.12 released
revision.change: Added support for Tab and TreeView gadgets.
Created a command-line version without Wimp support and added GCCSDK cross-compilation support.
Reduced memory usage and made uncovered Resource and Template bits round-trippable through hexadecimal output.
Added support for menu_GENERATE_HAS_BEEN_HIDDEN.

revision.author: John Tytgat / BASS
revision.title: Version 1.13 released
revision.change: Simplified parts of the source code.
Corrected the maximum-icons-per-window calculation that could otherwise corrupt memory.
Added a Unix-based regression test queue for binary-to-text and text-to-binary round-tripping.
Corrected a missing text_and_sprite.text: column in indirected text-and-sprite Template handling.
Made string allocation respect explicit limit values and warn when the limit is too small for the supplied text or sprite string.

revision.author: Phil Pemberton
revision.title: Portable command-line version
revision.change: Ported the command-line tool to Linux and other non-RISC OS systems, with the OSLib 7.00 headers adjusted so that structure layouts match the 32-bit file formats on 64-bit hosts.
Corrected strings containing top-bit-set characters being ended early on hosts where char is signed.
Removed leftover debugging output, and the abort after ten syntax errors.
Corrected compiler warnings found on 64-bit hosts.
Updated a stale test reference file, and added build instructions.

revision.author: Gerph
revision.title: Initial canonical CCres reference
revision.change: Created the canonical PRM-in-XML documentation for CCres, covering the standalone command-line tool, file recognition, the common text grammar, the Toolbox Resource textual format, and the Wimp Template textual format from the current implementation.

revision.author: Gerph
revision.title: Version 1.14 released
revision.change: Corrected Wimp icon button type names, such as wimp_BUTTON_RADIO, being rejected when followed by other icon flags.
Limited Resource file decoding to the size actually stored for each object and gadget, so that older, shorter gadgets and truncated object bodies no longer cause crashes.
Added support for OptionsWindow and UpdateCheck objects, and for the Scrollbar, ImageFileGadget, ColourSwatch, AMPlayer, MDNSService, URLImage and Divider gadgets.

Corrected heap corruption when converting Template text whose indirected title or icon buffers were larger than a fixed estimate, such as a window title buffer of 32 bytes or more in a window without icons.
Corrected string table overflow for very long strings and large buffers.
Made the warning for a too-small Template size value a warning only, so it no longer makes the conversion fail.

revision.author: Gerph
revision.title: Version 1.15 released
revision.change: Made errors in a text file make the conversion fail, with the field named in flag and value errors; white space around flags and values is now accepted, and over-long names are truncated with a warning.
Added the --skeleton and --describe options.
Added the field reference for every Resource and Template block, generated from the converter, with the flag and enumeration values each field accepts.
Described the layout of icons with text and a sprite, the window flag raising an event when the window is hidden, and the order in which fields must be given.

revision.author: Gerph
revision.title: Version 1.16 released
revision.change: Described the storing of an empty validation string as -1.
